text: Public Television (PT)
PT is based in country A and is a public sector business. PT broadcasts television
programmes, as well as operating an online streaming service throughout country A.
PT’s mission statement is:
‘Our vision is to target the mass market to strengthen the welfare and cultural health of
our country’. 5
The government of country A has introduced a law to improve diversity and equality in the
workplace. PT has been criticised for a lack of diversity and equality in terms of its female
employees, who make up 40% of its 20 000 employees (see Table 1.1).
Table 1.1 Employment statistics for PT in 2025
salary job satisfaction labour turnover 10
average for all employees $30 000 76% 12%
average for female employees $23 500 41% 20%
The directors of PT have agreed to implement a plan to improve diversity and equality,
which includes:
• Encouraging male employees to take parental leave. 15
• Offering free childcare for all employees with children under the age of five.
• Setting targets for the selection of female employees for all positions in PT, including
higher managerial positions.
• Ensuring all female employees are given equal access to training and development,
especially for the qualities intrapreneurs need for success. 20

text: Zorba’s Flowers (ZF)
Zorba had always had a passion for flower arranging. When he was made redundant from
his job as an engineer last year, he decided to use all of his savings to set up a flower shop
called ZF.
Although Zorba did not require any additional finance, he decided to write a business
plan before setting up ZF. Table 2.1 shows an extract from his business plan, showing the 5
planned expenditure for ZF.
Table 2.1 Planned expenditure for ZF
expenditure $
fixtures and fittings for the shop 10 000
rent (per month) 5 000 10
employees (per month) 3 000
inventory (per month) 7 000
delivery van (one needed) 20 000
Zorba opened ZF at the start of January 2026. However, Zorba encountered a number of
problems with Supply Chain Management during the first three months of ZF’s trading. 15
These included:
• Changeable weather conditions meant that Zorba could not always guarantee which
types of flowers would be available.
• ZF was often forced to work over-capacity at times of high demand.
• The inventory is perishable and can be easily damaged when transported. 20
At the end of the first three months of trading, Zorba realised that he had no working capital
left. The problem was that he had not been effectively managing his trade payables.
